takeaways.text: Revenue fell 1% to $12.8B and the operating loss widened to $1,964M from $1,016M a year ago, after a $943M restructuring and litigation charge. Excluding that charge and other adjustments, non-GAAP operating income was just $24M and non-GAAP EPS was $0.02 versus GAAP EPS of $(0.38). Intel answered with a $10B cost-reduction plan, a headcount cut of more than 15%, and a suspended dividend from Q4.
takeaways.title: The loss, and the reset it triggered

takeaways.text: Intel Foundry lost $2,830M on $4,320M of segment revenue, and only $77M of that revenue came from outside customers — down 67% YoY — the rest was wafers sold to Intel's own product groups. The product groups still earned $2,912M combined: Client Computing $2,497M, Data Center and AI $276M and Network and Edge $139M.
takeaways.title: Foundry lost more than the product groups earned

takeaways.text: Operating cash flow was $2,292M, but adjusted free cash flow of $8,155M was lifted by $5,863M of net partner contributions and incentives, mostly the Apollo joint venture for Fab 34 in Ireland. Intel paid $0.5B in dividends — its last before the suspension — and Q3 guidance is $12.5–13.5B of revenue with GAAP EPS of $(0.24).
takeaways.title: Cash flow flattered by a factory deal

verdict: Intel lost $1.6 billion in the second quarter on $12.8 billion of revenue, then suspended its dividend and announced a $10 billion cost-cutting plan with more than 15% of jobs to go.
